sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Phase 1 (1894-1906):** Characterized by **Moderate methods**—petitions, memorials, and appeals to the British authorities to secure rights for Indians as British subjects.
• **Phase 2 (1906-1914):** Emergence of **Satyagraha** (Truth-force) as a weapon of the weak; shift from constitutional agitation to direct action.
• **Core Philosophy:** Integration of **Ahimsa** (non-violence) and **Satyagraha** to challenge the 'Asiatic Registration Act' and the invalidation of non-Christian marriages.
• **Key Metric:** The transition from 'Petitioning' to 'Passive Resistance' marked the birth of Gandhi's unique political methodology.

The 'Black Act' requiring Indians to register and carry identification cards; triggered the first major Satyagraha campaign.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Great March (1913):** Protest against the £3 tax on ex-indentured Indians and the invalidation of non-Christian marriages.
• **Gandhi-Smuts Agreement (1914):** Resulted in the abolition of the £3 tax and recognition of Indian marriages.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges:** Internal divisions among Indian merchants and indentured laborers; severe state repression.
• **Solutions:** Building a unified platform (NIC) and using the press (Indian Opinion) to bridge class gaps.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym:** 'N-I-P-T' (Natal, Indian Opinion, Phoenix, Tolstoy).
• **Decoded Meaning:** N (Natal Congress 1894) -> I (Indian Opinion 1903) -> P (Phoenix Farm 1904) -> T (Tolstoy Farm 1910).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Natal Indian Congress' with the 'Indian National Congress'. Ensure you distinguish that NIC was founded in South Africa, not India.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Political Laboratory' to describe South Africa in the context of Gandhi's later success in the Indian freedom struggle.

keyTakeaways: Gandhi's South African phase was the training ground for his later mass movements in India.
The shift from moderate petitioning to Satyagraha was the most significant ideological evolution.
Institutional building (NIC, Phoenix Farm) was as critical as the protest movements themselves.
